page: Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It also includes 2097 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 10% tier. However, the high core count compensates in parallel workloads, with multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores reaching average levels. Memory performance is a notable strength, with read-only large block memory bandwidth (256MB) ranking in the top 25% at 215.58 GB/sec, while small block read and large block write bandwidth remain average. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs strongly, placing in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M64s offers high resource density, particularly in memory allocation, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require cutting-edge single-thread compute speeds. The instance is suited for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive caching layers, and enterprise applications. It is also capable of handling moderate multi-threaded tasks such as static web serving, software compilation, and basic text or image processing, though it is less optimal for single-threaded processing or heavy LLM text generation.
